neighbours.label: Token right before a predicted 'short'/'shorten' (multilingual): fires on the word preceding shorten/short, e.g. 'may' in 'may shorten the duration', 'is' in 'stay is shortened', 'Keep baths' before 'short'
fire: Several small trials suggest that zinc lozenges may shorten the duration of a common cold by about a day.
With the new surgical technique, the average hospital stay is shortened from five days to just two.
Dermatologists advise patients with eczema to keep baths short and to use lukewarm rather than hot water.
The committee voted to cut the meeting short after the fire alarm went off twice.
Taking the express highway could shorten your commute by nearly twenty minutes each morning.
Doctors found that the antiviral drug may shorten recovery time in otherwise healthy adults.
Please keep your speech short, because twelve other guests are also giving toasts tonight.
The editor asked me to shorten the article to fit on a single printed page.
quiet: According to one review, zinc lozenges may reduce the severity of a common cold.
Thanks to better anesthesia, most patients now leave the hospital feeling less pain.
People with eczema should moisturize right after bathing every evening, experts say.
Board members agreed to extend the meeting after the budget debate ran over.
Driving along the scenic coastal road will lengthen your trip, but the views are worth it.
In the trial, the antiviral drug caused mild nausea in some older adults.
At the reception, guests hoped the speeches would be warm and personal.
My publisher wants the article expanded with two more interviews and a chart.

notes: Label and sentences written blind by a Claude subagent from the card text alone (prompt: haiku_labeler/prompt.md, identical for Haiku, Sonnet and Opus); one retry on mechanical checks. Part of a Haiku/Sonnet/Opus comparison on the same 48 poles.
